title: Disk Steward macOS evidence monitor

intent.statement: A macOS user can leave Disk Steward running as a lightweight menu-bar app, understand material disk growth, export trustworthy evidence for Codex or Claude, and query the same evidence through a read-only local MCP integration.

success_evidence.description: A signed-development build launches as a menu-bar utility; left-click opens a compact status board and right-click exposes Export, Settings, About, and Quit.
The app measures whole-volume capacity while collecting bounded detailed evidence for configured roots and registered agent process trees.
Evidence identifies path, time, size delta, actor and agent session when observable, and labels exact, tool-linked, inferred, or unknown attribution without guessing.
A user can export a portable, integrity-manifested evidence bundle containing a concise Codex brief and machine-readable detailed records.
Codex and Claude can query sanitized evidence through the same read-only local MCP executable without rescanning the disk.
Monitoring remains useful without restricted privileges and enables exact Endpoint Security provenance only when entitlement and user authorization are available.
The app records no file contents, provides explicit privacy exclusions and retention limits, and performs no deletion or cleanup mutation in this intent.
Automated and reproducible checks demonstrate buildability, evidence correctness, regression safety, bounded idle resource use, and recovery from unavailable monitoring components.

constraints: Use a native Swift-first macOS architecture and keep the continuously running footprint bounded.
Prefer macOS 13 or newer, Swift 6, AppKit for status-item mouse behavior, SwiftUI for presented UI, SQLite for local evidence, and the official Swift MCP SDK.
Treat Endpoint Security entitlement approval as an external dependency and preserve a functional FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
Keep MCP read-only and avoid an externally reachable HTTP listener.
Do not persist file contents, secrets, or unbounded raw write-event streams.
Every attribution statement must carry method and confidence.
Generated evidence and databases must have deterministic retention and size controls.
non_goals: Automatic deletion, cache purging, process termination, or destructive MCP tools.
Cloud synchronization, accounts, telemetry, or a hosted backend.
Detailed monitoring of external, network, Time Machine, or cloud-placeholder volumes by default.
Guaranteeing Apple Endpoint Security entitlement approval.

assumptions.statement: The development machine has a compatible Xcode and Swift toolchain for a macOS 13+ Swift 6 application.
A native project layout can package the menu app, a local MCP executable, and later a system extension without introducing a second application language.
Endpoint Security entitlement may be unavailable or delayed, so exact system-wide attribution cannot be a prerequisite for the standard product path.
A stdio MCP executable can serve both Codex and Claude while delegating sanitized queries to the local app-owned evidence service.

evidence: All changes are inside the declared EndpointSecurity schemas, fixtures, contract tests, and provenance architecture document.

verified_primary_nodes.title: Implement optional Endpoint Security observer

evidence: All implementation changes are confined to TASK-410's Package.swift, Extensions/DiskStewardEndpoint, Sources/DiskStewardCore/EndpointBridge, Tests/DiskStewardEndpointTests, and Config/Entitlements scope.
The observer event inventory contains only notification-oriented create, write, close, rename, unlink, exec, and exit families. No authorization callback or blocking decision API is represented.
EndpointMonitoringScope applies watched-root and exclusion-prefix policy before normalization or bridge delivery; the fixture test proves an excluded path is discarded.
ProtectedEndpointBridge validates team, bundle, app group, designated requirement, and a constant-time challenge digest. A spoofed peer is rejected without event delivery.
Normalized events retain PID plus process-start time and file device/inode identity. Exact eligibility requires complete identity, size, deadline, and gap-free input.
The bounded buffer constrains both event count and byte use, coalesces only compatible consecutive writes, records dropped ranges, and downgrades after overload or sequence discontinuity.
Denied, crashed, overloaded, and missing-entitlement states keep the metadata fallback active and carry a visible reason; retry state is bounded. The runtime never attempts to bypass macOS security.
Four focused endpoint tests, all 92 repository tests, Swift build, macOS-targeted Xcode build, and git diff --check passed.

No live entitlement claim is made. Apple-granted entitlement, release signing, system-extension activation, and user approval remain explicit distribution prerequisites; the deterministic fixture transport is the available acceptance evidence on this host.

verified_primary_nodes.title: Implement exact and inferred provenance engine

evidence: All changed files are within the node's Core Provenance, App ProvenanceUI, Provenance tests, and Provenance fixtures scope.

Create, grow, and rename golden cases require matching operation, normalized destination path, observation time, logical and allocated deltas, complete file identity, deadline, and gap-free privileged input before claiming exact.

A task link requires one authenticated session covering the event time and ancestry from the full writer identity to its registered process. The PID-reuse test proves a same-number/different-start process does not inherit the task.
Incomplete privileged evidence with a unique task is tool-linked, historical evidence is inferred without a current task assertion, and path-only evidence with a source gap is unknown.
Overlapping workspaces, mismatched byte deltas, mismatched privileged observations, and gapped path hints do not select an actor or task.

Claims retain typed references to Endpoint Security event IDs, metadata events, FSEvents IDs, PID/start-time ancestry, session registration IDs, and historical records, each describing exactly what it supports.
UI, export, and MCP channels return the same ProvenancePresentationRecord. The board item renders that record without recalculating or upgrading evidence.
Models contain metadata, identities, causal references, and limitations only; no file-content field or content inspection exists.
Five focused provenance tests, all 97 repository tests, Swift build, and git diff --check passed.

verified_primary_nodes.title: Enforce privacy, resource, permission, and release controls

evidence: All changed files are inside the node's explicit Package, Privacy, ResourceControl, Onboarding, SafetyTests, PerformanceTests, operations, Distribution, Signing, and evidence scopes.

Five hundred generated secrets placed independently in paths, commands, and executable locations were absent from JSON-encoded filtered metadata. Exclusions omit complete subtrees; basename and SHA-256 path modes are deterministic. No file-content or environment input exists.

The resource budget matches the existing 512 MiB evidence-store cap, while existing retention tests cover bounded raw/rollup retention and forced eviction. Resource measurement history is capped and tested at 10,000 inputs.

A 100,000-event unique-path storm completed in 1.342 seconds with at most 512 retained events under a 256 KiB configured queue. Every discarded event was counted, hasGap was set, and the budget evaluator required backpressure.
Not-requested, pending, denied, and unavailable permission states all report standard monitoring active, exact provenance unavailable, and no retry/bypass behavior.

Evidence preservation is the default uninstall plan and deletion requires an explicit export-then-delete decision. Six focused integration tests prove dry-run immutability, recoverable backups, owned-entry removal, and preservation of unrelated settings and evidence.

Development preflight validates package, entitlements, app group, and hardened-runtime configuration. Release preflight exits 65 on the placeholder team before signing; the runbook requires entitlement approval, provisioning, signing, notarization, clean-host activation, and uninstall verification.

Five safety tests, two performance tests, six focused integration tests, all 104 repository tests, Swift build, macOS-targeted Xcode build, distribution development preflight, and git diff --check passed.

The audit does not treat test-process timing as signed-product CPU/memory evidence. Production resource sampling and signed-host measurements remain a declared release check rather than an unsupported claim.

verified_primary_nodes.title: Audit advanced provenance and final intent

evidence: The gate adds only its independent final increment test and residual-limitations report inside the allowed Final test and GATE-490 evidence scopes.

The test launches the built DiskStewardApp executable with its supported UI-smoke route and verifies status launched, accessory activation policy, snapshot availability, active IPC, left-click status board, right-click utility menu, and stable menu commands.
A live volume snapshot populates the board, current snapshot export succeeds, and watched/excluded roots plus retention settings survive reload.
A real temporary watched-root write becomes an inferred metadata event while a configured excluded subtree produces no event. SQLite integrity and the 10 MiB test retention cap are verified.

The exact fixture joins matching path, operation, time, logical/allocated deltas, file identity, PID/start identity, and one authenticated session; Endpoint Security, metadata, ancestry, and session source references are all present and identical across UI/export/MCP projections.
Denied optional permissions retain standard monitoring and disable exact provenance. A gapped unprivileged observation stays unknown with no actor, and a stopped IPC service fails closed.
The evidence bundle uses basename paths, declares no contents/environment, includes required limitations, and every payload matches its byte count and SHA-256 manifest digest.

The built MCP connector initializes over the private socket, exposes exactly seven read-only tools with no delete tool, returns the persisted event through get_provenance, and contains no forbidden content/environment/token/secret/password keys.

Sensitive path/command/executable values do not survive filtering, excluded paths are absent, the database remains below cap, the healthy resource measurement passes declared budgets, and separate stress evidence proves bounded overload accounting.
After swift package clean, the full package rebuilt and all 105 tests passed. The macOS-targeted Xcode scheme and development distribution preflight also passed, and git diff --check is clean.

The gate explicitly distinguishes fixture exactness from unavailable live entitlement evidence and leaves signing, notarization, activation lifecycle, and signed-artifact resource measurements as release limitations rather than weakening fallback acceptance.

decisions.question: What is the smallest honest delivery ladder from an empty repository?
decisions.choice: Deliver four cumulative runnable increments: snapshot/export menu app; persistent evidence recorder; agent-queryable MCP integration; advanced exact provenance with fallback.
alternatives: Treat project scaffolding as an increment
decisions.rationale: Each selected rung gives the user a launchable, meaningful scenario and isolates storage, integration, and restricted-entitlement risks behind independent gates.

decisions.question: Which application stack should be primary?
decisions.choice: Swift 6 with a small AppKit NSStatusItem shell, SwiftUI presentation, a shared Swift core, and SQLite persistence.
alternatives: Tauri with a Rust core and web UI
Pure MenuBarExtra without AppKit status-item event handling
decisions.rationale: The selected stack directly accesses macOS monitoring, service-management, signing, and menu APIs while minimizing continuous runtime and cross-language boundaries.

decisions.question: How broadly should monitoring persist detailed evidence?
decisions.choice: Track whole-volume capacity everywhere accessible, but persist detailed evidence only for configured roots, registered agent process trees, and bounded investigation windows.
alternatives: Scan the whole disk only when asked
decisions.rationale: The hybrid model preserves unexplained-growth detection and agent attribution without creating an unbounded privacy and resource burden.

decisions.question: How should Codex and Claude access evidence?
decisions.choice: Bundle one read-only Swift MCP stdio executable that delegates to the app-owned evidence service over a protected local IPC boundary.
alternatives: Expose a persistent localhost HTTP server
Give each agent direct SQLite access
Maintain separate Codex and Claude implementations
decisions.rationale: One connector minimizes duplication and attack surface while keeping database ownership, sanitization, and retention inside the application.

decisions.question: How should exact system-wide attribution depend on Endpoint Security?
decisions.choice: Implement it as an advanced capability with explicit confidence semantics and retain a useful FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
alternatives: Block the whole product on entitlement approval
decisions.rationale: Entitlement approval is external and cannot be guaranteed; the product must remain honest and useful in its absence.

decisions.question: Should the first product intent perform cleanup?
decisions.choice: No; it will explain, export, and recommend while all MCP tools remain read-only.
decisions.rationale: Evidence trust and attribution accuracy must be established before introducing destructive operations.
